name: Taylor Wimpey plc
executive_summary:
Taylor Wimpey is a leading UK volume housebuilder trading at a material discount to tangible net asset value, with net cash, an undrawn £600m revolving credit facility, and a shareholder-return framework targeting 7.5% of net assets annually. The quantitative screen rates the name **strong buy** (12/22 models; P/E 11.8, P/B 0.71, yield 4.9%), driven by cheapness, dividend, and balance-sheet metrics. The central debate is whether headline valuation compensates for cyclical margin pressure, rising cladding remediation provisions (£243.8m exceptional charge in FY2025), and weakening free-cash-flow cover of distributions—the screen itself flags an FCF basis mismatch (filing £126.5m vs TTM £276.8m) and adjusts the signal to **buy**. Management guides FY2026 adjusted operating profit to ~£400m on softer pricing and cost inflation, with net cash expected to fall further at H1 2026.

---
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Taylor Wimpey offers a classic **asset-backed cyclical** profile: FY2025 tangible NAV of **117.6p** (FY2024: 123.8p) against a screen-implied P/B of **0.7**, plus **£342.6m net cash** at year-end and minimal drawn debt. The screen passes Graham Defensive, Schloss Low P/B, Deep Value, Earnings Yield, Low P/E + High Yield, High Dividend Yield, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, Composite Value, and Financial Health—three of four factor families (cheapness, dividend, risk). Business quality indicators from filings are solid: five-star HBF customer service (score 4.24 under revised methodology), industry-leading CQR **4.96**, and a **~77k-plot** short-term landbank with **~133k** strategic pipeline plots.

Operational momentum is real—FY2025 completions rose **6%** to 11,229 homes and revenue grew **13%** to **£3,844.6m**—but adjusted operating margin compressed to **10.9%** (from 12.2%), below medium-term targets of 16–18%. The updated distribution policy (5.0% of net assets as ordinary dividend plus 2.5% via dividend or buyback) still commits to **≥£250m** annual returns; FY2025 total distribution was **~£322m** (7.62p ordinary dividend plus **£52m** buyback). Return on net operating assets ticked up to **11.0%** but remains far below the **>20%** medium-term ambition. The screen’s strong-buy case rests on balance-sheet optionality and mean-reversion in margins/volumes; our filing review confirms the asset cushion but highlights that **statutory earnings and cash generation are being eroded by non-recurring charges**, limiting clean earnings-yield confirmation.

financial_review:
### Primary source: annual RNS filings

**FY2024 (year ended 31 Dec 2024; RNS 27 Feb 2025)**

| Metric | FY2024 | FY2023 | YoY |
|--------|--------|--------|-----|
| Revenue | £3,401.2m | £3,514.5m | (3.2)% |
| Operating profit | £416.2m | £470.2m | (11.5)% |
| Operating margin | 12.2% | 13.4% | (1.2)ppt |
| Profit before tax | £320.3m | £473.8m | (32.4)% |
| Profit for the year | £219.6m | £349.0m | (37.1)% |
| Adjusted basic EPS | 8.4p | 9.9p | (15.2)% |
| TNAV per share | 123.8p | 127.1p | (2.6)% |
| Net cash | £564.8m | £677.9m | (16.7)% |
| Ordinary dividend | 9.46p | 9.58p | (1.3)% |
| RONOA | 10.9% | 12.6% | — |
| Cash conversion | 74.9% | 61.4% | — |

Completions fell modestly to **10,593** (2023: 10,848). Exceptional costs of **£98.2m** (cladding provision increase **£68.9m**, Winstanley/York Road JV loss **£13.6m**) drove the gap between adjusted and statutory earnings. Adjusted gearing (net cash less land creditors) was **1.4%**. Directors confirmed **going concern** and **five-year viability** under a severe downside (10% volume decline, 5% price cut, £150m one-off cost).

**FY2025 (year ended 31 Dec 2025; RNS 5 Mar 2026)**

| Metric | FY2025 | FY2024 | YoY |
|--------|--------|--------|-----|
| Revenue | £3,844.6m | £3,401.2m | +13.0% |
| Adjusted operating profit | £420.6m | £416.2m | +1.1% |
| Adjusted operating margin | 10.9% | 12.2% | (1.3)ppt |
| Profit before tax | £146.5m | £320.3m | (54.3)% |
| Profit for the year | £100.4m | £219.6m | (54.3)% |
| Adjusted basic EPS | 8.0p | 8.4p | (4.8)% |
| TNAV per share | 117.6p | 123.8p | (5.0)% |
| Net cash | £342.6m | £564.8m | (39.3)% |
| Ordinary dividend | 7.62p | 9.46p | (19.5)% |
| RONOA | 11.0% | 10.9% | +0.1ppt |
| Cash conversion | 63.7% | 74.9% | — |

Exceptional costs totalled **£243.8m**: cladding provision **£225.8m** (mainly cavity-barrier remediation behind brickwork/render) and CMA voluntary commitments **£18.0m**. Completions rose to **11,229**; **71** UK outlets opened (+29% YoY). Provisions on the balance sheet increased to **£492.1m** (from £306.7m). Net finance swung to **£30.3m expense** (from £2.3m income), reflecting lower average cash balances. **FY2026 guidance:** UK completions **10,600–11,000** (40% H1-weighted); adjusted operating profit **~£400m**; cladding cash spend **~£150m**; H1 2026 net cash **~£0–50m**.

### Trend assessment

Revenue and volumes recovered in FY2025, but **margin quality deteriorated**: gross margin fell to **17.1%** (19.1%) on softer opening order-book pricing, low single-digit build-cost inflation, and a **£20.0m** London contractor defect charge. Adjusted operating profit was essentially flat despite **+6%** completion growth—operating leverage is working in reverse near term. Net cash has fallen **£335m** over two years (FY2023 £677.9m → FY2025 £342.6m), driven by dividends, land/WIP investment, land-creditor paydown, and exceptional cash outflows. TNAV per share has drifted lower for two consecutive years.

### Interim filing gap

**No interim, half-year, or trading-update regulatory bodies** are indexed. Recent operational updates (e.g. trimmed completion guidance, distribution reductions) appear only in news summaries referencing an H1 2026 earnings call (1 Aug 2026)—these figures are **not verified from primary interim filings** in this pack.

### Yahoo fallback (cash flow only)

Where filing bodies do not provide a consolidated cash-flow statement in extract form, **Yahoo `financials_annual.json`** shows FY2025 **free cash flow of £126.5m** (operating cash flow £133.2m; dividends paid £330.4m). This corroborates the screen’s flagged **FCF/dividend coverage tension** and basis mismatch versus TTM FCF (£276.8m per screen). Balance-sheet figures in Yahoo (total assets £6,066m; inventory £5,271m; equity £4,187m; cash £419m at FY2025) are broadly consistent with RNS net-asset and net-cash disclosures; inventory-heavy working capital remains structurally large (~87% of total assets).

risks_and_flags:
**Regulatory and remediation:** Cladding fire-safety provisions remain the dominant earnings drag. FY2025 added **£225.8m** (203 buildings in scope per FY2024 disclosure; intrusive FRAEW assessments continue). FY2026 guided cash spend of **~£150m** will further reduce net cash. The Building Safety Levy (implementation postponed to Oct 2026) and Future Homes Standard (expected H1 2026) add future cost uncertainty; management states it is mitigating via land buying but quantification is incomplete.

**Cyclical demand:** Principal risks B (mortgage availability/housing demand) and C (materials/subcontractor costs) are rated moderate. FY2025 order book entering 2026 was **lower** (£2,182m vs £2,283m prior-year equivalent at 1 Mar 2026). Cancellation rate **14%**; sales rate **0.74** per outlet/week (vs 0.76). Southern England affordability and first-time-buyer access remain constrained.

**Governance / competition:** The CMA information-sharing investigation closed **30 Oct 2025** without infringement findings; Taylor Wimpey paid **£15.8m** toward a £100m industry affordable-homes contribution plus fees (**£18.0m** exceptional). Voluntary conduct commitments apply. Residual reputational overhang is low but not zero.

**Pension:** TWPS showed an IAS 19 **surplus of £107.0m** (FY2025) and technical-provisions surplus on the 2022 triennial valuation, yet **IFRIC 14** requires a **£17.8m** balance-sheet liability (committed PFP payments up to £12.5m/year from 2029–2035 if deficits emerge). Not a near-term cash drain (£7.1m annual contributions) but limits surplus recognition.

**Liquidity and leverage:** Headline net cash (**£342.6m**) plus **£600m** undrawn RCF provides ample covenant headroom; going concern and viability statements explicitly reference **£1,030m** combined liquidity (FY2025). However, guided H1 2026 net cash of **£0–50m** and adjusted gearing rising to **4.3%** (from 1.4%) signal tightening if the downcycle persists. Viability stress test (10% volume cut, 10% price cut, £150m one-off in 2026) still passes without drawing the RCF.

**Competitive / market sentiment:** Investegate short-position data (Mar 2026) shows elevated hedge-fund interest—Janus Henderson **1.53%**, Two Sigma **1.18%**, AQR **0.68%**—suggesting a meaningful cohort of market participants bearish on near-term earnings or dividend sustainability.

**Accounting quality:** Statutory EPS **2.8p** vs adjusted **8.0p** in FY2025; recurring "exceptional" cladding charges make screen earnings-yield metrics less reliable. Cash conversion fell to **63.7%**.

RiskTags: regulatory, cyclical, governance, pension, competitive, liquidity, litigation, accounting

research_rationale: Filings confirm the screen’s cheapness and balance-sheet resilience, but rising cladding charges, margin compression, and FCF shortfall versus distributions weaken the clean strong-buy case pending interim filing verification and FY2026 cash trajectory.
